outcome: Since 26 January 2024 the conjecture has acquired one claimed full proof (L. Zeng, arXiv:2508.06123, 8 Aug 2025; unrefereed, and the step giving the lower bound lambda_1 >= n was not visible to me), a restricted-class equality (Jimenez, Tapia Chinchay and Zhou, arXiv:2405.20545, published Rev. Mat. Iberoam. 2026: lambda_1 = m when max|A| <= sqrt(m)), several verifications on families of surfaces in S^3 (Kapouleas–McGrath Nov 2024; Saavedra–Castrillon Vasquez Apr 2026, conditional; Pigazzini Sep 2026), numerical checks and a criterion on one family (Perdomo 2025–2026), and quantitative bounds strictly above n/2 (Zhao Mar 2026; Yu Jun 2026). The Wikipedia article still says the problem is unsolved as of 2026, and the 2026 papers of Yu and Pigazzini describe it as open.
problem_asks: (1) For every closed (compact, boundaryless) embedded minimal hypersurface Sigma of the round unit sphere S^{n+1}, (2) the first nonzero eigenvalue lambda_1 of the Laplace–Beltrami operator on Sigma (3) equals n, the dimension of Sigma. Parts: the claim is universal over all dimensions n (the statement as given to me says only 'an embedded minimal hypersurface of S^{n+1}'; 'closed' is supplied from the literature, where Yau's conjecture is stated for closed hypersurfaces). The claim has two halves: the upper bound lambda_1 <= n, which is classical (Takahashi: the coordinate functions restricted to Sigma are eigenfunctions with eigenvalue n), and the lower bound lambda_1 >= n, which is the conjectural content. Equality is required, not only a bound. Surfaces (n = 2, minimal surfaces in S^3) are a named subcase in the literature.

events.what_happened: Wikipedia credits Almgren (1966) with the genus-0 case of the conjecture: embedded minimal 2-spheres in S^3 (which are great spheres, where lambda_1 = 2 trivially). Primary paper not opened; this is taken from the Wikipedia article only.
events.delivers: lambda_1 = 2 for embedded minimal 2-spheres in S^3 (genus 0 only), per Wikipedia.
events.remains: All genus >= 1 surfaces in S^3 and all dimensions n >= 2 for hypersurfaces of higher codimension-one type in general.
events.directly_checkable: A great 2-sphere in S^3 has first nonzero eigenvalue 2 (its coordinate functions); the classification is what Wikipedia reports.
events.direction: Cuts in the conjectured direction (lambda_1 = n = 2) for genus 0.

events.what_happened: Choi and Wang proved that the first nonzero eigenvalue of a closed embedded minimal hypersurface in S^{n+1} is at least n/2, via Reilly's formula and a harmonic extension of the eigenfunction (J. Differential Geom. 18 (1983) 559–562, as cited in the Zeng and Yu bibliographies). The 1983 paper is not on arXiv and was not opened; the result is described in the opened abstracts of Jimenez et al. (arXiv:2405.20545), Zhao (arXiv:2603.20890) and Duncan–Sire–Spruck (arXiv:2308.12235).
events.delivers: lambda_1 >= n/2 for all closed embedded minimal hypersurfaces of S^{n+1}, all n. A partial result: a lower bound of half the conjectured value.
events.remains: The gap between n/2 and n, i.e. the equality lambda_1 = n.

checked_by.where: Cited as J. Differential Geom. 18 (1983) 559–562 in the bibliography of arXiv:2508.06123 (opened as HTML via summary); not opened directly

events.direction: Partial, toward lambda_1 = n: a lower bound in the direction the conjecture points, but weaker than the conjectured value.

events.what_happened: Xuanguo Huang posted arXiv:math/0411079, titled 'The First Eigenvalue for Compact Minimal Embedded Hypersurface in S^{n+1}(1) (n>=3) is n', claiming lambda_1 = n for compact, closed, orientable embedded minimal hypersurfaces in S^{n+1} for n >= 3. The current version's abstract (v3, 2 Jun 2005) reads, in full: 'I'm sorry that there is a gap in this paper.' The paper is 50 pages; its body was not read. A search snippet from a Colombian journal (revistas.unal.edu.co, not opened) reports that Huang's preprint claimed the result for all dimensions except surfaces and gives the range inconsistently as n > 4 in one place and n >= 4 in another. The paper was not withdrawn as far as the arXiv page shows.
events.revisions: v1 4 Nov 2004 (20 KB); v2 30 Mar 2005 (20 KB); v3 2 Jun 2005 (1 KB, current; comment: '50 pages without figures, minor corrections at page 31 and page 48. New version').
events.delivers: As titled: lambda_1 = n for closed embedded minimal hypersurfaces in S^{n+1} with n >= 3. Surfaces (n = 2) are not claimed in the title. The author's own abstract says the paper has a gap, so what is delivered is a claim the author concedes is incomplete.
events.remains: Surfaces in S^3 (n = 2), and any part of n >= 3 covered by the acknowledged gap. Whether the gap is closed is not established by any source I found.
events.time_since_posted: about 22 years, no published verification found; the 2025 Zeng preprint's visible introduction does not cite it
events.doubts: The author's abstract concedes a gap ('I'm sorry that there is a gap in this paper'). I did not find where the gap is located, since the body was not read. Secondary sources disagree on the dimension range (n > 4 versus n >= 4, and 'all dimensions except surfaces' in the Colombian snippet). The arXiv abstract's concession is the only direct statement on the status of the argument.
events.direction: Claims the conjectured value lambda_1 = n in dimensions n >= 3: the direction Yau conjectured, for that range.

events.what_happened: Jaigyoung Choe and Marc Soret verified the conjecture for embedded minimal surfaces in S^3 invariant under a finite group of reflections in great spheres, in particular the Lawson surfaces and the Karcher–Pinkall–Sterling surfaces: lambda_1 = 2 for these. The venue is given as Indiana Univ. Math. J. 58(1) (2009) 269–281, title 'First eigenvalue of symmetric minimal surfaces in S^3', in the Yu 2026 bibliography (arXiv:2606.10962, opened as HTML). The paper itself was not opened; its claim is described in the Wikipedia article, in Zhao's 2023 arXiv summary, and in a search snippet of Brendle's survey.
events.delivers: lambda_1 = 2 for the Lawson surfaces and the Karcher–Pinkall–Sterling surfaces (surfaces in S^3 with reflection symmetry). The class is confined to these symmetric surfaces.
events.remains: All other embedded minimal surfaces in S^3, including those of genus >= 2 without the symmetry, and all dimensions n >= 3.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper (2009), as cited by later papers
checked_by.where: Cited in arXiv:2606.10962 bibliography (opened as HTML); journal page not opened

events.direction: Cuts in the conjectured direction (lambda_1 = 2) for the reflection-symmetric class.

events.what_happened: Zizhou Tang and Wenjiao Yan, 'Isoparametric foliation and Yau conjecture on the first eigenvalue', arXiv:1201.0666, first posted 3 Jan 2012 (v3 17 Jul 2012); published J. Differential Geom. 94(3) (2013) 521–540. They prove the conjecture for minimal isoparametric hypersurfaces of S^{n+1} and show the first eigenvalues of focal submanifolds equal their dimensions in the non-stable range.
events.revisions: v1 3 Jan 2012; v2 6 Jan 2012; v3 17 Jul 2012 (current, 34 KB). Journal: J. Differential Geom. 94(3) (2013).
events.delivers: lambda_1 = n for every closed minimal isoparametric hypersurface in S^{n+1}. A full resolution for that class.
events.remains: All closed embedded minimal hypersurfaces that are not isoparametric, which is the general conjecture.

checked_by.where: arXiv:1201.0666 abstract (opened); journal publication per the Zeng and Yu bibliographies and a search snippet of the Project Euclid record

events.direction: Cuts in the conjectured direction (lambda_1 = n) for the isoparametric class.

events.what_happened: Simon Brendle, 'Embedded minimal tori in S^3 and the Lawson conjecture', arXiv:1203.6597, first posted 29 Mar 2012 (final v3 18 Sep 2012, noted as to appear in Acta Mathematica 211(2) (2013) 177–190). It proves that every embedded minimal torus in S^3 is congruent to the Clifford torus, answering Lawson (1970). Through the Montiel–Ros reduction this gives the genus-1 case of the conjecture. The proof is a maximum-principle argument on the surface, not a spectral one.
events.revisions: v1 29 Mar 2012; v2 2 Apr 2012; v3 18 Sep 2012 (final, 'to appear in Acta Mathematica').
events.delivers: Shape result: every embedded minimal torus in S^3 is the Clifford torus. Together with lambda_1 = 2 for the Clifford torus, this gives lambda_1 = 2 for every genus-1 embedded minimal surface in S^3. Restricted to genus 1.
events.remains: Genus >= 2 embedded minimal surfaces in S^3, and all higher dimensions.

checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted the paper for publication (to appear, Acta Math. 211(2) 2013 per the arXiv comment and the Zeng bibliography)

events.direction: Cuts in the conjectured direction (lambda_1 = 2) for genus 1. The eigenvalue statement is inferred from the Clifford shape by the reduction in the Wikipedia article and in the Zhao 2023 summary; Brendle's abstract itself says nothing about eigenvalues.

events.what_happened: Zizhou Tang, Yuquan Xie and Wenjiao Yan, 'Isoparametric foliation and Yau conjecture on the first eigenvalue, II', arXiv:1211.2533, submitted 12 Nov 2012 (revised 19 Feb 2014; the arXiv page says to appear in J. Funct. Anal.). It estimates all eigenvalues of focal submanifolds with six distinct principal curvatures, proves lambda_1 equals the dimension in two of four unsettled OT–FKM-type cases, and says the result 'may be regarded as a generalization of Yau's conjecture'.
events.delivers: First eigenvalues of certain focal submanifolds of isoparametric families equal their dimensions in two listed OT–FKM-type cases. It is about focal submanifolds, not the closed hypersurface statement, and does not claim the conjecture for hypersurfaces of S^{n+1}.
events.remains: The hypersurface statement of the conjecture in general, and the isoparametric cases the paper does not cover.
events.direction: Neighbouring result: a related eigenvalue statement for focal submanifolds of isoparametric families. It does not move the hypersurface conjecture, though the authors call it a generalization.

events.what_happened: Jonathan J. Zhu, 'Minimal hypersurfaces with small first eigenvalue in manifolds of positive Ricci curvature', arXiv:1512.00105, submitted 1 Dec 2015 (revised 16 Oct 2016). It constructs deformations of the hemisphere (n >= 2) that keep Ric >= n and minimal boundary but lower the boundary's first Laplace eigenvalue, and argues that resolving Yau's conjecture would need more geometric input than a Ricci lower bound.
events.delivers: Counter-examples to a Ricci-curvature route for the boundary eigenvalue inside positively curved ambient manifolds, not in the round sphere. It is a neighbouring setting and does not settle the sphere case.
events.remains: The round-sphere conjecture, unchanged.
events.direction: Neighbouring: a different ambient setting. It is evidence about methods, not about the statement.

events.what_happened: Zhongyang Sun, 'Partial result of Yau's Conjecture of the first eigenvalue in unit sphere S^{n+1}(1)', arXiv:1607.08306, submitted 28 Jul 2016 (v2 1 Aug 2016). The abstract says the author 'partially solve[s] Yau's Conjecture' (Corollary 1.2) under an integral condition on the eigenfunction, the quoted identity being integral of |grad u|^2 = (n+1) times integral of u^2, which Corollary 1.3 says is natural. The corollary statements were not read.
events.delivers: lambda_1 = n for closed embedded minimal hypersurfaces satisfying an additional integral hypothesis on the first eigenfunction (exact class not read). A restricted case.
events.remains: The conjecture without that integral hypothesis.
events.doubts: The extra hypothesis is not one the conjecture assumes. The abstract does not establish that it holds automatically. The exact corollary statement was not read.
events.direction: Partial: a restricted case under an extra eigenfunction hypothesis.

events.what_happened: Yuhang Zhao, 'First eigenvalue of embedded minimal surfaces in S^3', arXiv:2304.06524, first posted 13 Apr 2023 (v3 19 Jul 2023). Proves lambda_1 >= 1 + eps_g for embedded minimal surfaces of genus g in S^3, with eps_g > 0 depending only on g. A search snippet says it was published in Acta Math. Sinica in 2026 (DOI 10.1007/s10114-026-5125-6); that page was not opened.
events.revisions: v1 13 Apr 2023; v2 23 Apr 2023; v3 19 Jul 2023. Journal publication 2026 per search snippet.
events.delivers: lambda_1 >= 1 + eps_g for embedded minimal surfaces in S^3 of genus g: an improvement on Choi–Wang's 1, depending on genus. Partial; does not reach lambda_1 = 2 for general genus.
events.remains: lambda_1 = 2 for every embedded minimal surface in S^3 of every genus; the explicit form of eps_g was not read.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper (2026), per a search snippet

events.direction: Partial, toward lambda_1 = 2 for surfaces in S^3: a genus-dependent improvement on the Choi–Wang bound.

events.what_happened: Jonah A. J. Duncan, Yannick Sire and Joel Spruck, 'An improved eigenvalue estimate for embedded minimal hypersurfaces in the sphere', arXiv:2308.12235, posted 23 Aug 2023 (one version). The main estimate is lambda_1 >= n/2 + a_n (Lambda^6 + b_n)^{-1}, with a_n, b_n explicit dimensional constants and Lambda an upper bound for |A|. Published in Int. Math. Res. Not. 2024(18) 12556–12567 per the Yu 2026 bibliography (journal page not opened).
events.revisions: Single version posted 23 Aug 2023. IMRN 2024 publication per the Yu 2026 bibliography.
events.delivers: An explicit, quantitative improvement on n/2 for all closed embedded minimal hypersurfaces of S^{n+1}, with constants depending on n and on the bound Lambda for |A|. Partial; does not reach lambda_1 = n.
events.remains: lambda_1 = n for all such hypersurfaces.

checked_by.where: arXiv:2606.10962 bibliography (opened as HTML); IMRN page not opened

events.direction: Partial, toward lambda_1 = n: a quantitative improvement on Choi–Wang with an explicit dependence on the second fundamental form.

events.what_happened: Mikhail Karpukhin, Robert Kusner, Peter McGrath and Daniel Stern, 'Embedded minimal surfaces in S^3 and B^3 via equivariant eigenvalue optimization', arXiv:2402.13121, posted 20 Feb 2024. They build embedded minimal surfaces in S^3 (and free boundary ones in B^3) by maximising Laplace and Steklov eigenvalues under discrete symmetry groups. The abstract does not mention Yau's conjecture or the value lambda_1 = 2 for these surfaces.
events.delivers: Existence of new minimal surfaces in S^3 as eigenvalue maximisers under symmetry. The abstract does not state lambda_1 = 2 for them. Whether the body establishes lambda_1 = 2 for these surfaces is not known to me; the body was not read.
events.remains: The conjecture for these surfaces (not established by the abstract) and in general.
events.doubts: A maximiser of lambda_1 realised as a minimal surface in a sphere would, by Nadirashvili-type arguments, have its first eigenfunctions among the coordinate functions. That would bear on the conjecture for these surfaces. I could not confirm this from the abstract, and the body was not read, so this is flagged rather than recorded as a verification.
events.direction: Neighbouring. Unclear from the abstract whether it bears on lambda_1 = 2 for its surfaces.

events.what_happened: Asun Jimenez, Carlos Tapia Chinchay and Detang Zhou, 'A lower bound for the first eigenvalue of a minimal hypersurface in the sphere', arXiv:2405.20545, posted 31 May 2024 (one version). For closed embedded minimal hypersurfaces of S^{m+1} with Lambda = max |A|, they prove lambda_1 > m/2 + m(m+1)/(32(12 Lambda + m + 11)^2 + 8), and that lambda_1 = m when Lambda <= sqrt(m). Proof follows Choi–Wang's Rayleigh quotient for the harmonic extension. The journal version is Rev. Mat. Iberoam. 42(1) (2026) 261–278, DOI 10.4171/RMI/1587, per search snippets; the EMS page was not opened.
events.revisions: v1 31 May 2024 only. Peer-reviewed journal version 2026 (Rev. Mat. Iberoam.).
events.delivers: lambda_1 = m for closed embedded minimal hypersurfaces with max |A| <= sqrt(m): the conjecture established for that class. For all other such hypersurfaces only the quantitative bound above.
events.remains: Hypersurfaces with Lambda > sqrt(m), where only the quantitative inequality holds; and the general conjecture.

checked_by.who: Referees of Revista Matematica Iberoamericana (refereed journal)
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted and published the paper (2026), per search snippets

events.doubts: The equality is conditional on the second fundamental form bound Lambda <= sqrt(m), so it is restricted to a class and not dimension-only. A search snippet (of an unidentified 2026 paper, not opened) says the gap in this bound tends to zero as max |A| tends to infinity, so the bound does not depend on m alone.
events.direction: Partial, but with a true equality on a restricted class (Lambda <= sqrt(m)). Elsewhere a quantitative bound toward lambda_1 = m.

events.what_happened: Nikolaos Kapouleas and Peter McGrath, 'New minimal surface doublings of the Clifford torus and contributions to questions of Yau', arXiv:2411.00613, posted 1 Nov 2024 (one version; 26 pages, no figures). The abstract says they verify Yau's first-eigenvalue conjecture for (i) all minimal surface doublings of the equatorial two-sphere constructible by their earlier general theorem and (ii) all Clifford-torus doublings constructed in the paper. The verification itself was not read. The Wikipedia article's preprint list describes the paper as not peer-reviewed as of its date.
events.delivers: lambda_1 = 2 for two families of embedded minimal surfaces in S^3: doublings of the equatorial two-sphere from the authors' general theorem, and the Clifford-torus doublings constructed in the paper. Surfaces only (n = 2), restricted to those families.
events.remains: All other embedded minimal surfaces in S^3 and all higher dimensions.
events.time_since_posted: about 23 months, with no refereed publication found
events.doubts: Attribution conflict: the Wikipedia article credits the equatorial-doubling case to Kusner and McGrath (AJM 2024, arXiv:2011.06884), while the Kapouleas–McGrath abstract claims the verification for its own family. The arXiv abstract of arXiv:2011.06884 does not mention Yau's conjecture, so the Wikipedia credit is not supported by that abstract. The verification in the body was not read.
events.direction: Cuts in the conjectured direction (lambda_1 = 2) for two families of surfaces in S^3.

events.what_happened: Lingzhong Zeng (single author; no affiliation shown on arXiv), 'The First Eigenvalue of Embedded Minimal Hypersurfaces in the Unit Sphere I: Yau's Conjecture', arXiv:2508.06123, posted 8 Aug 2025 (one version; comment '3 figures. Any comment is welcome'). Theorem 1.3 claims: for a closed embedded minimal hypersurface Sigma in S^{n+1}, lambda_1 = n. The abstract describes the method as a carefully built minimizing sequence in a suitable Sobolev space plus the variational principle, presented as an affirmative resolution of Yau's conjecture, and derives rigidity theorems. The arXiv HTML (v1) was read only through WebFetch summaries: Section 8 concludes that a limit u* of trial functions u_beta = x_i(1 - beta^{-1} e^{-beta d^2}) has Rayleigh quotient n and is an eigenfunction for lambda_1 = n. No journal publication, erratum, comment, referee report or expert critique was found.
events.revisions: Single version (v1, 8 Aug 2025) as listed on the arXiv abstract page.
events.delivers: Claims the full conjecture: lambda_1 = n for every closed embedded minimal hypersurface of S^{n+1}, all n. The upper bound lambda_1 <= n (Takahashi) is classical. What the paper must establish beyond it is lambda_1 >= n. The visible portions I could read establish only the upper bound (see doubts).
events.remains: Nothing, if the claim is correct. As far as I could read, the step giving lambda_1 >= n is not in the portions that the summaries covered, so the delivered content is the upper bound plus an unproved equality.
events.time_since_posted: about 14 months (to 13 Oct 2026), with no journal, erratum, comment, critique or expert commentary found
events.doubts: (1) The gap in the argument as I read it. A test-function sequence with Rayleigh quotients tending to n gives lambda_1 <= n, which Takahashi's theorem already gives. Concluding lambda_1 = n needs lambda_1 >= n: that no admissible function has Rayleigh quotient below n. The Section 8 argument, as summarised to me, derives R[u*] = n for a limit u* and concludes that u* is an eigenfunction for lambda_1 = n, which presupposes that u* minimises the Rayleigh quotient. I did not find that step in the summaries, and a WebFetch summary asked directly for every numbered Theorem, Lemma and Proposition found no independent lambda_1 >= n statement (its only lower bound was Choi–Wang's n/2, cited in the introduction). The summaries covered the page in two passes (characters 0–100,000 and 100,000–142,494), with a truncated end. This is a reading through a summariser, not my own reading of the raw text, and it is the first thing a judging pass should check. (2) Silence. Yu (9–10 Jun 2026) and Pigazzini (7–11 Sep 2026) both describe the conjecture as open or verified only in special cases, and neither cites Zeng in the visible text (their reference lists were partly unread). The Wikipedia article, which by its 2026 reference list was updated after 11 Sep 2026, still says the conjecture is unsolved and does not mention Zeng. (3) The introduction (summary) says the problem 'remained unresolved for non-isoparametric cases', which is consistent with the claim but does not engage with Huang's 2004 preprint or the Duncan–Sire–Spruck and Jimenez et al. bounds. (4) The author has one earlier paper on the isoparametric bi-Beltrami problem (arXiv:1612.01255, 2016); that is background, not evidence of error.
events.direction: Claims the conjectured value lambda_1 = n for all closed embedded minimal hypersurfaces of S^{n+1}: the direction Yau conjectured, in full.

events.what_happened: Oscar Perdomo, 'The stability index and Yau's conjecture for Carlotto–Schulz minimal hypertori', arXiv:2508.09104, posted 12 Aug 2025 (v2 15 Sep 2025). For the Carlotto–Schulz minimal embeddings of S^{n-1} x S^{n-1} x S^1 in S^{2n}, the abstract states that Yau's conjecture holds for these examples if and only if the solution of z'' + a_n(t) z' + (2n-1) z = 0 with z(0)=1, z'(0)=0 satisfies z'(T) > 0 (T and a_n determined by the immersion). It also gives a stability index bound of at least n^2+4n+3 (v1 gave 3n+6, corrected in v2).
events.revisions: v1 12 Aug 2025; v2 15 Sep 2025 (corrects the multiplicity formula to a product and the index bound; 'no other results are affected' per the comment).
events.delivers: An if-and-only-if criterion for Yau's conjecture on this one family of hypertori, for every n > 1. The abstract does not say whether the criterion is verified for each n, so as read it is not an unconditional verification.
events.remains: Unconditional verification for these hypertori (unless the criterion is checked), and every other hypersurface.
events.doubts: The v1 contained errors (the multiplicity formula and the index bound) that v2 corrected. The criterion's verification is not stated in the abstract.
events.direction: Criterion for the conjecture on one family; neither a counterexample nor an unconditional verification.

events.what_happened: Yuhang Zhao (sole author), 'The first eigenvalue of embedded minimal hypersurfaces in the unit sphere', arXiv:2603.20890, v1 21 Mar 2026, v2 24 Mar 2026 (47 pages). The abstract proves lambda_1 > m/2 + c, with c > 0 depending on m and on the maximum and minimum norms of the second fundamental form; when the norm is constant, c depends only on m. The abstract says 'This improves Choi and Wang's previous result' and that one can improve Choi–Wang directly without proving Chern's conjecture. It does not address Yau's conjecture's status in the visible text.
events.delivers: A quantitative improvement on n/2: lambda_1 strictly above m/2 by an explicit constant depending on m and on the second fundamental form. Not equality.
events.remains: lambda_1 = m for all such hypersurfaces.
events.time_since_posted: about 7 months, no refereed publication found
events.direction: Partial, toward lambda_1 = m: a quantitative bound, not equality.

events.what_happened: Julieth Saavedra and A. J. Castrillon Vasquez, 'Symmetries and the First Laplace Eigenvalue of Lawson Surfaces', arXiv:2604.17731, posted 20 Apr 2026 (one version). Motivated by Yau's conjecture, for Lawson surfaces xi_{m,k} in S^3 with m and k even they show lambda_1 = 2 follows once a natural topological obstruction for invariant nodal sets in the fundamental patch is verified. The abstract does not say the obstruction is verified.
events.delivers: Conditional: lambda_1 = 2 for Lawson surfaces with m, k even, given a topological obstruction that the abstract does not say is verified. Not unconditional.
events.remains: Unconditional lambda_1 = 2 for those surfaces; all other Lawson surfaces; the general conjecture.
events.doubts: Conditional on an obstruction the abstract does not say is verified. The body was not read.
events.direction: Cuts in the conjectured direction (lambda_1 = 2) for a family, conditionally.

events.what_happened: Jonas Henkel and Emilio A. Lauret, 'Hodge Laplacian on 1-forms of homogeneous 3-spheres', arXiv:2605.05406, posted 6 May 2026. The abstract computes the first eigenvalue of the Hodge Laplacian on 1-forms for homogeneous metrics on SU(2) and SO(3), and says: 'The formal proof of this result was autonomously discovered by an advanced AI model'. This is a different operator and a different problem from Yau's conjecture (Laplace–Beltrami on minimal hypersurfaces). It is recorded because the AI search surfaced it. A search snippet of a Cambridge seminar page (not opened) names ChatGPT 5.4 Pro for the same work; that naming is not the authors' statement and is not used in ai.systems.
events.delivers: Does not bear on Yau's conjecture: a result on the first eigenvalue of the Hodge Laplacian on 1-forms of 3-spheres.
events.remains: Yau's conjecture entirely.
events.doubts: Different problem: the abstract mentions a 'First Eigenvalue Conjecture' for the Hodge Laplacian on 1-forms, not for minimal hypersurfaces. Not to be confused with Yau's conjecture.
events.direction: Neighbouring problem (a different operator). Does not move Yau's conjecture.

systems.name: an advanced AI model
systems.what_it_did: Per the authors' abstract, autonomously discovered the proof of the result (for a different problem, the Hodge Laplacian on 1-forms). The model is not named by the authors.
systems.basis_quote: The formal proof of this result was autonomously discovered by an advanced AI model

events.what_happened: Jinhong Yu (sole author), 'On the First Eigenvalue of Embedded Minimal Hypersurfaces in the Unit Sphere', arXiv:2606.10962, v1 9 Jun 2026, v2 10 Jun 2026. The abstract says the author establishes an improved lower bound for lambda_1 slightly better than Duncan–Sire–Spruck. The HTML introduction (read via summary) states that the conjecture 'has been verified for certain special cases': Lawson and Karcher–Pinkall–Sterling surfaces (Choe–Soret) and isoparametric hypersurfaces (Tang–Yan). Theorem 1.2, as summarised: lambda_1 >= n/2 + n^2 / (27 (sqrt(Lambda^2 + 2n) + Lambda)^2), Lambda = max |A|. Zeng (2508.06123) is not cited in the visible text.
events.delivers: A quantitative lower bound above n/2 for closed embedded minimal hypersurfaces. Not equality.
events.remains: lambda_1 = n in general.
events.doubts: The formula for Theorem 1.2 comes from a WebFetch summary of the HTML, which itself flagged that the final line uses sqrt(Lambda^2 + 2 lambda_1) where the theorem uses sqrt(Lambda^2 + 2n). The PDF text layer could not be read. The formula should be checked against the source.
events.direction: Partial, toward lambda_1 = n: a quantitative bound.

events.what_happened: Oscar Perdomo, 'The stability index and Yau's conjecture for Carlotto–Schulz minimal hypertori, part II', arXiv:2606.16980, posted 15 Jun 2026 (one version). The abstract proves a multiplicity lower bound 2n+1+n^2 for the eigenvalue -(2n-1) of the stability operator for the Carlotto–Schulz embedding, conjectures a formula for the stability index (n > 2) and 27 for n = 2, and states that Yau's conjecture is 'numerically verified' for 2 <= n <= 260.
events.delivers: Numerical verification of Yau's conjecture for the Carlotto–Schulz hypertori with 2 <= n <= 260. Not a proof.
events.remains: All n > 260, and a proof for every n.
events.directly_checkable: The numerical check is of the Yau criterion for the specified n; a reader can rerun it from the paper's method, but the method was not read.
events.doubts: The conjecture for n > 2 on the stability index is itself conjectural, and the Yau verification is numerical only.
events.direction: Supports the conjecture numerically for one family; does not prove it.

events.what_happened: Alexander Pigazzini, 'Yau's conjecture for the stacked Clifford tori of Wiygul', arXiv:2609.07423, posted 7 Sep 2026 (v2 11 Sep 2026; 33 pages). The abstract claims lambda_1 = 2 for every closed embedded minimal surface from Wiygul's construction with N >= 2, k, l >= 1 and every sufficiently large m (genus k l m^2 (N-1) + 1). The method, per the abstract: the Choe–Soret reflection lemma reduces to invariant functions; analytic inputs are a channel inequality on a cylinder and a Poincare inequality on a perforated torus. The introduction says: 'To our knowledge the conjecture is open in every dimension n >= 2' and 'equality has been established on explicit families'.
events.revisions: v1 7 Sep 2026; v2 11 Sep 2026 (references updated to J. Differential Geom. 114 (2020) 467–549 for Wiygul; minor corrections, results unchanged).
events.delivers: lambda_1 = 2 for a family of embedded minimal surfaces in S^3 (Wiygul's stacked Clifford tori) for every N >= 2, k, l >= 1 and sufficiently large m. The abstract does not quantify 'sufficiently large m'.
events.remains: All other embedded minimal surfaces in S^3, the small-m cases of the family, and all higher dimensions.
events.time_since_posted: about 5 weeks, no refereed publication found
events.doubts: Only the abstract and introduction were read; the body was read only up to 100,000 characters of a 166,459-character HTML page and the later sections and reference list were not read. The threshold for m is not given in the abstract. The Wikipedia article cites it as a preprint.
events.direction: Cuts in the conjectured direction (lambda_1 = 2) for a family of surfaces in S^3.

events.what_happened: Montiel and Ros (1986) showed that Lawson's conjecture on embedded minimal tori in S^3 is the torus case of Yau's conjecture (per a search snippet of the Brendle survey and the Wikipedia article's known-cases discussion). The paper was not opened.
events.delivers: A reduction, not a resolution: Lawson's torus question is the torus case of the conjecture. It establishes no new value of lambda_1 by itself.
events.remains: The conjecture in every case.
events.direction: Structural: relates the tori case of the conjecture to Lawson's question. Does not move lambda_1.

disputes.summary: The Wikipedia article credits the proof for doublings of the equatorial two-sphere to Kusner and McGrath (AJM 2024; arXiv:2011.06884). The arXiv abstract of arXiv:2011.06884 (v2, 2022) does not mention Yau's conjecture. Kapouleas and McGrath (arXiv:2411.00613, Nov 2024) claim the verification for their own family of equatorial doublings.

Zeng (arXiv:2508.06123, Aug 2025) claims the full conjecture. The Wikipedia article (whose reference list includes a Sep 2026 preprint) says the conjecture remains unsolved as of 2026 and does not mention Zeng. Yu (Jun 2026) and Pigazzini (Sep 2026) describe the conjecture as open or verified only in special cases, without citing Zeng in the visible text.

The strict inequality lambda_1 > n/2 over Choi–Wang's bound is credited variously in search snippets to Brendle, to Barros–Bessa, and to Xu, Chen, Zhang and Chen. The attribution is not settled across these sources and was not checked against the primary papers.

Huang's 2004 preprint claims the result for n >= 3, but its own abstract concedes 'there is a gap in this paper'. Secondary sources give inconsistent dimension ranges (n > 4 versus n >= 4; 'all dimensions except surfaces').

summary: Nothing in the sources I read settles the conjecture cleanly, and the most important open question concerns the one claimed proof. Zeng's arXiv preprint (8 Aug 2025) claims lambda_1 = n for every closed embedded minimal hypersurface of S^{n+1}. In the visible text, the argument as summarised to me concludes lambda_1 = n from a limit of test functions with Rayleigh quotient n, which by itself gives only lambda_1 <= n (Takahashi already gives that). The step giving lambda_1 >= n was not visible in any summary I received. The reading comes from WebFetch summaries of the HTML (142,494 characters, read in two passes, with a truncated end), not from the raw text, so it should be checked against the paper. No journal, erratum, critique or citing paper engaging with Zeng was found in about 14 months. Yu (June 2026) and Pigazzini (September 2026) both describe the conjecture as open and do not cite Zeng in the visible text, and the Wikipedia article still says unsolved. Huang's 2004 claim for n >= 3 is conceded in its own abstract to contain a gap. Before 2024, the conjecture was settled for the isoparametric class (Tang–Yan, JDG 2013), for genus-1 surfaces in S^3 (Brendle, Acta 2013), and for the Lawson and Karcher–Pinkall–Sterling surfaces (Choe–Soret, 2009). Since 2024: Jimenez, Tapia Chinchay and Zhou (RMI 2026, peer-reviewed) prove equality lambda_1 = m for closed embedded minimal hypersurfaces with max|A| <= sqrt(m), a restricted class, plus a quantitative bound elsewhere; Kapouleas–McGrath (Nov 2024) claim equality for two families of doublings in S^3; Perdomo (Aug 2025) gives an if-and-only-if criterion for one family of hypertori, and numerical checks for 2 <= n <= 260 (June 2026); Saavedra and Castrillon Vasquez (April 2026) show lambda_1 = 2 for Lawson surfaces with m, k even conditional on an unverified topological obstruction; Pigazzini (September 2026) claims lambda_1 = 2 for Wiygul's stacked Clifford tori for sufficiently large m; Zhao (March 2026) and Yu (June 2026) prove quantitative bounds above n/2. Where a call was close: whether Jimenez et al. count as settling part of the conjecture (yes for the stated class, by my reading of the abstract) and whether the Kapouleas–McGrath and Pigazzini families count as settling anything (they are restricted families of surfaces in S^3, not the general case). On AI, I found no source naming an AI system in connection with this conjecture. The one AI-credited result near it, Henkel and Lauret (6 May 2026), concerns the Hodge Laplacian on 1-forms of 3-spheres, a different problem, and is recorded as a discarded neighbour. Lab announcements and trackers I surveyed (OpenAI's May and August 2026 announcements, Tao's Erdos tracker, a Google Erdos sweep) do not mention this problem. The AI search was run on search snippets only and nothing in the sources I read credits an AI system with any mathematics for this conjecture.
competing_reading: The strongest case for treating Zeng's claim as a settled full resolution: it is a single, explicit theorem with a stated method, by an author who has previously published on the isoparametric version of the same circle of ideas (arXiv:1612.01255). The lower-bound step may simply be in the part of the paper I could not read, since the summaries were partial and the Section 8 text was truncated. Choi–Wang's n/2 and the subsequent quantitative bounds do not rule out equality, and a resolution would not necessarily show up in later papers within 14 months. Against that: the only inequality I could find in the visible text is the upper bound lambda_1 <= n, which is classical, and the later specialist papers (Yu, Pigazzini, Zhao) still treat the conjecture as open without citing the claim. The strongest case for treating Jimenez et al. as a settled restricted case: a peer-reviewed journal (RMI 2026) accepted an explicit equality on the class max|A| <= sqrt(m). The strongest case against counting it: that class is restricted by a hypothesis on the second fundamental form, and the equality is not dimension-only.
what_would_settle_it: For Zeng: a reading of the full Section 8 (and any lemma establishing lambda_1 >= n) by a specialist in minimal hypersurfaces or spectral geometry, a referee report or journal decision, an erratum or a published rebuttal, or a later paper that cites Zeng and either uses or refutes the lower bound. A Lean formalisation of the lower-bound step would also settle it, but none exists that I found. For Jimenez et al.: the published RMI text, to confirm the Lambda <= sqrt(m) statement and its hypothesis. For Kapouleas–McGrath and Pigazzini: the body of each paper and a specialist's reading of the families' verification. For Huang: the location of the gap named in the 2005 version's abstract.

incomplete: (1) Zeng (2508.06123): the decisive lower-bound step was not read directly. I read the HTML only through WebFetch summaries (two passes over 142,494 characters, with the final part reported as truncated), and the summaries disagreed on whether the proof is complete. The reading that the visible text gives only an upper bound must be checked against the full text. (2) Yu (2606.10962): Theorem 1.2 is from a summary of the HTML, and the PDF could not be read. (3) Pigazzini (2609.07423): only the first 100,000 characters were read; the remaining sections, the acknowledgements and the reference list were not. (4) Not opened directly: the Choi–Wang 1983 paper, Choe–Soret 2009, Almgren 1966, Montiel–Ros 1986, the journal pages for Tang–Yan, Brendle, Duncan–Sire–Spruck, Jimenez et al., Zhao 2023 and Sun 2016 (the arXiv abstract pages were opened for the last four). Their claims are taken from abstracts, bibliographies, search snippets or the Wikipedia article, and the record says which. (5) Bodies not read: Huang (50 pages; the location of the gap is unknown), Kapouleas–McGrath, Saavedra–Castrillon Vasquez, Perdomo parts I and II (the criterion's check), Karpukhin–Kusner–McGrath–Stern, Sun (corollary statements), Duncan–Sire–Spruck and Zhao 2026. (6) Reference lists of the 2026 papers were partly unread, so 'not cited' means 'not in the visible text'. (7) AI search covered search snippets and lab news, not primary lab announcements; the Cambridge seminar and the Quanta article were not opened. (8) The record does not cover the Chern-conjecture route beyond the Wikipedia reference, and it does not judge which event the problem's status rests on.
